objects: objects selected or paid as costs
events: nonmana activated ability is put on the stack
control of an ability source changes
state_writes: paid mana, life, energy, loyalty, and object costs
source zone after discard, sacrifice, or exile cost
costs: selected sacrifice, discard, return, and crew objects
timing: requires priority unless a mana ability is used during payment
summoning-sickness restriction for creature tap and untap costs
once-per-turn restriction persists on the object
targets: represented target schemas are selected and validated during activation
choices: represented modes, targets, cost objects, and mana payments
hidden_information: private cards and cost candidates remain projected only to the entitled seat
apnap: opponent-made activation choices are not yet represented
layers: effective abilities, source types, keywords, and restrictions are consulted where implemented
copy: copied or acquired activation restrictions lack generic ability provenance
control_change: per-object once-per-turn history survives control change
zone_change: ordinary cost zone changes use the authoritative move path
source_leaves: a paid nonmana activated ability remains on the stack after its source leaves

implementation.component: abilities.parse_activated_abilities plus CommanderEngine activation availability, cost-payment, and stack paths

known_blockers: the Oracle parser recognizes selected cost and activation-instruction grammars rather than every activated ability
full CR 601.2b-i announcement, mode, target, division, cost-modification, mana, and rollback behavior is not shared universally
hidden-zone reveal timing and public record behavior are incomplete
opponent-made activation modes, targets, and simultaneous choices are absent
cost-altering activated abilities do not use a generic prospective-cost effect model
continuous prohibitions and activation instructions outside selected text predicates are incomplete
acquired-ability provenance does not distinguish identically worded restricted abilities
illegal activation rollback is not represented as a universal transaction
